full_judgment:
4. Defendant No.5 contested the suit and his case is that the suit land originally belonged to Surendra; Md Rafiuddin got the land from Surendra on 22-5-16. Rafiuddin paid rents to the landlord and taxes to the Municipality. It is the further case of this defendant that Surendra became malik dokhalker by way of purchase on 1-9-20. Rafiuddin and Surendra took 'namjaree' settlement and Rafiuddin acquired projayee satta' on 7-9-21. The name of Menatosh was recorded in RS Khatian as bondobesti right; he exclusively possessed the suit land. Abdur Rahman gave lease of the suit land to his wife, Samana Kha tun and he handed over possession to her on 19-3-57 and thereafter, Abdur Rahman died, Samana Khatoon became owner of the suit land having title and possession. Abdur Rahman had no right in the suit land and Samana Khatoon had right and possession over the suit land exclusively since 1949. Thereafter, Samana sold the suit land to Abdul Huq on 15-3-69. Her husband, Abdur Rahman used to look after the affairs of the suit property and plaintiffs did not demand any partition and are not entitled to have any portion of land of the suit property. This suit has been filed fraudulently and this defendant is entitled to realise rents from tenants of RS Plot Nos. 321 and 322 and on these pleadings, this defendant prayed for dismissal of the suit. 

 The appellate Court held that through Exhibit-H no transfer was made. I concur with this view. Other document of title of defendant No.1 is patta, Exhibit G. This Exhibit G was made in 1949. By this Exhibit G, defendant wanted to prove that Abdur Rahman Sowdagar settled some properties with defendant No.1 in 1949. But it appears that Abdur Rahman got settlement of the land mentioned in Exhibit G from Rafiuddin on 15-7-57. If Abdur Rahman got the land in 1957 then how he could settled the said land in favour of defendant No.1 by Exhibit G in 1949. This is also against the settle principle of law that before acquiring title one cannot settle the land to another and if he settle such land, then it also stands as void. Defendant No.1 could make out a case under section 43 of the Transfer of Property Act, i.e feeding of title by estoppel but defendant No. 1 did not do so. The argument was forwarded from the side of defendant-petitioner that name of defendant No.1 has been recorded in RS Khatian in 1960 but recording the name of defendant No.1 is not on the strength of Exhibit-G or H, but on the strength of her inheritance i.e. defendant No.1 is legally entitled to two annas share from Abdur Rahman Sowdagar and her name is recorded to that effect. On consideration of Exhibits G and H, I find that these are not documents of title and, as such, if these two deeds are left aside from consideration, then defendant No.1 would get only 2 annas share as heir as wife of Abdur Rahman and in the suit property. In partition Suit, plaintiffs and defendants stand on equal footing and no weakness of plaintiffs or defendants, ipso facto, give saham to anyone. The defendant No.1 is to prove acquisition of property through Exhibits G and H to have partition of the suit land to the extent of 14 annas share in the suit property. In that view of the matter, I find that the learned Additional District Judge committed no illegality in decreeing partition Suit to the extent of 14 annas share. I also hold that since plaintiff of Other Suit No.7 of 1972 acquired no title by purchase as her vendor acquired no title by wasiatnama and patta, the suit i.e. Other Suit No.7 of 1972, filed by Ambia Khatoon for ejectment of Abdus Salam, who is a plaintiff in Partition Suit No. 63 of 1970, has been rightly dismissed. In that view of the matter, I find no substance in this Rule.
